name: What is the biggest reason custom home builds in LA go over budget?

mainEntity.name: What is the biggest reason custom home builds in Los Angeles go over budget?
mainEntity.text: What is the biggest reason custom home builds in Los Angeles go over budget?

acceptedAnswer.text: The biggest budget overruns in Los Angeles custom home construction usually come from site conditions and scope changes. Many homeowners budget for the house itself but underestimate grading, demolition, retaining walls, soils work, utility upgrades, structural engineering, and city requirements. Finish upgrades also create large swings, especially in kitchens, baths, windows, doors, cabinetry, and flooring. Another common issue is choosing a design before doing full due diligence on the lot, which can reveal expensive surprises later. Change orders are especially costly once framing and finishes are underway because they affect labor, sequencing, and materials already ordered. A strong budget should separate hard construction costs from soft costs, permits, design, consultants, and a contingency reserve. Homeowners in LA should ask for allowances that match the actual design level and request a clear list of exclusions. If a bid is far below others, it may be missing major items rather than offering a better price.
acceptedAnswer.description: The most common reason custom home budgets go over in Los Angeles is underestimating site complexity and allowing too little contingency. Hillside grading, retaining walls, foundation upgrades, utility work, plan changes, and finish upgrades can all add major cost. Change orders after construction starts are another major budget driver.
